result.title: Physics-Constrained Neural ODEs for Learning Traffic Dynamics and Trajectories from Road Entry/Exit Times
result.summary: We consider the problem of learning microscopic traffic dynamics and reconstructing vehicle trajectories from section entry/exit timestamps (EET) recorded by cameras and from the positions of a probe vehicle leading the platoon. The dynamics are difficult to recover as each vehicle's position is measured only at two points, and its trajectory between them is unknown. By combining Neural ODEs with a local density approximation, we learn a follow-the-leader model whose speed--density relation is a neural network. With such sparse data, an unconstrained network may learn physically unrealistic relations, such as negative speeds or non-zero speeds on a fully congested road. We therefore introduce a normalization that, applied to a monotone neural network with a learned regime change, enforces the endpoint conditions, guaranteeing an admissible speed--density relation while provably retaining the ability to approximate any admissible one. We validate the method on first- and second-order simulations, recovering the speed--density relation of the first-order model and reconstructing the trajectories of both models, with mean maximum position errors of 2.50~m and 2.51~m, respectively, on a 125~m road segment. On real-world ring-road data, the proposed model still yields an admissible relation, whereas both baselines violate the constraints; the large spread in the data, however, highlights the limitations of a first-order model with homogeneous driver behaviors.

AI.brief_summary: 该文用 Neural ODE 结合局部密度近似，从路段进出口时间戳与探针车位置学习跟驰模型，令速度—密度关系由神经网络表示，并用带可学习状态切换的单调网络归一化保证物理可行的端点条件，在仿真与实测环道数据上重建车辆轨迹。
AI.relevance_reason: 其从极稀疏端点观测推断连续隐状态轨迹、并以结构约束保证所学关系可容许的做法，可能为 LVR 中 latent 轨迹监督与状态转移合理性的建模提供核查线索，但领域距离较远、迁移需较多论证。
